title: Git Hub grant database operations
responsibility: Store versioned GitHub grants and coordinate refreshes and revocation with conditional updates.

inputs.name: d1GrantStore.db
inputs.description: D1-compatible database handle; queries run only when the returned store methods are called.

inputs.name: d1GrantStore.records
inputs.description: Validator whose grantState(row) turns a row found by read() into the grant state that read() returns. The file calls it only in read() and only for an existing row, and no try/catch wraps the call.

outputs.name: EXPIRE_GRANTS
outputs.description: String constant holding an UPDATE for auth_github_grants that tombstones each row with revoked_at still NULL and expires_at at or before its single ? placeholder: it erases the token, refresh and lease columns, increments generation and sets revoked_at to expires_at. This file only exports the string, and rows are never deleted, so a generation never repeats.
examples: UPDATE auth_github_grants SET token_cipher = '', token_expires_at = NULL, refresh_cipher = NULL, refresh_expires_at = NULL, refreshing_until = NULL, generation = generation + 1, revoked_at = expires_at WHERE expires_at <= ? AND revoked_at IS NULL

outputs.name: d1GrantStore
outputs.description: Store object with read, connect, lease, rotate, revoke and revokeLeased methods; connect, lease, rotate and revokeLeased resolve to true when a row matched and false otherwise, and revoke resolves with no value. read resolves to { generation: 0, grant: null, refreshingUntil: null } when no row exists for the actor.

errors.name: TypeError
errors.description: connect, lease, rotate and revokeLeased read properties of their record or lease argument synchronously before any query is sent, so a null or undefined argument throws a TypeError from the call itself.

errors.name: db error
errors.description: An error from db.prepare(...), .bind(...), .first() or .run(), including a TypeError when db is null or undefined, makes the store method that made the call reject with that error, because the file has no try/catch.

errors.name: records.grantState error
errors.description: read() rejects with any error raised while calling records.grantState(row) for an existing row, because the file does not catch it.
